attempts.summary: On node1, built an LVM-backed XFS filesystem at /srv/data (loop-device-backed VG vg_data/LV lv_data, since the node had no spare block device), populated application data, created an LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap), modified/corrupted the live data, and used lvconvert --merge to restore the exact pre-modification content (verified via sha256 diff). A systemd unit (srv-data-loop.service) attaches the loop device and activates the VG at boot so the setup persists across restarts; fstab mounts /srv/data with a dependency on that unit. An initial ordering-cycle bug in the unit was found after the first restart and fixed; a second restart proved the corrected unit auto-recovers the mount, LVM state, and data, and the restore procedure still works afterward. A fresh snapshot was left in place for ongoing recoverability.
